question: What is the Shema, and where is it found?

choices.A: The central Jewish declaration of faith ('Hear, O Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD alone'), found in Deuteronomy 6:4
choices.B: The Ten Commandments given to Moses on Mount Sinai, found in Exodus 20
choices.D: The opening verse of the book of Genesis declaring God as creator

teaching.title: The Shema
teaching.body: 'Shema Yisrael, Adonai Eloheinu, Adonai Echad' — 'Hear, O Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD alone (or, the LORD is one)' (Deut 6:4). This is the foundational declaration of Jewish monotheism, recited twice daily by observant Jews. Jesus cites it as the greatest commandment (Mark 12:29-30). The NT writers, who were monotheistic Jews, began to include Jesus within the Shema — Paul's 1 Corinthians 8:6 reworks Deut 6:4 to include 'one Lord Jesus Christ' alongside 'one God the Father,' a stunning early Christological move.
refs: NT Wright, Paul and the Faithfulness of God
